key_points: Growth signals are mixed: the Fed describes solid activity driven by AI capex, but June payrolls rose only +57k, GDPNow is a stale 1.3%, and the staff trimmed its GDP outlook with downside risks.
Consumer sentiment is depressed at 49.5, though it is rebounding. Claims of 215k show no layoff wave, so this is a slow-growth expansion rather than an accelerating one.
With 2y and 10y yields near 1-year highs on hawkish repricing, a softening growth impulse tilts modestly toward lower yields and some bull steepening over 1-3 months.

AI investment and earnings momentum support equities. The growth backdrop is not recessionary, so I lean mildly bullish on the S&P while expecting HY spreads near their tights to drift slightly wider over 3 months.

Weaker foreign growth and the U.S. growth-rate edge narrowing argue for a slightly softer dollar. The Middle East de-escalation removes energy demand support, so I am mildly bearish on oil over longer horizons.
Low VIX and tight spreads leave little room for further improvement if growth data disappoint, so I hold a small upward tilt for vol over 3 months.
Headline CPI running ~4.2% y/y and core PCE ~3.4% y/y with +0.3% monthly core prints: underlying inflation is sticky and broadening, per the minutes.
WTI fell ~23% in a month after the US-Iran MoU, so upcoming June/July headline prints should soften via gasoline, offsetting core stickiness in market pricing.

The 2-year at its 99th percentile already prices a hawkish Fed (hike priced for mid-2027); headline disinflation gives mild downside skew to front-end yields over 1-3 months, favoring modest steepening.
10y breakevens at 2.24 (10th percentile) look low relative to realized inflation and sticky core; with oil stabilizing, slight upside bias.
Fed has dropped its easing bias and a few members argued for hikes, capping how far yields can fall; net yield edge is small.
Equities supported by earnings/AI and falling energy costs; inflation risk is the main threat if core re-accelerates, so only a mild upward tilt.
Labor market is stable, not tightening: June payrolls +57k (soft headline), unemployment dipped to 4.2%, claims 215k near lows — no recession signal, supporting tight credit spreads and equities.
Wage growth decelerating (AHE 3.4% y/y, down 0.5pp; ECI 3.4%) — FOMC says labor is not a source of inflation, limiting the case for hikes driven by labor.
2y yield at 99th percentile already prices hawkish Fed; labor data unlikely to push further, slight downward tilt to front-end yields over 1-3 months and mild steepening.
Low year-on-year payroll growth (~42k/month) and low dynamism (falling job-finding rate) are a latent downside risk, modestly lifting VIX/spread risk at longer horizons from depressed levels.
Labor lens offers little edge on oil, gold, dollar and breakevens; kept near 0.50.
Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75% with easing bias removed and a few participants already arguing for hikes; July 29 meeting very likely a hold with hawkish tone.

2y at 4.21 sits ~55bp above effective funds rate and at 99th percentile of its range: market already prices a hawkish path, so further upside requires hike pull-forward; oil's 23% drop and soft payrolls (+57k) argue for modest mean reversion over 1-3m.
Curve flattened to 5th percentile on front-end repricing; if hike pricing fades, bull steepening is the likelier direction over 3m.

Headline inflation should ease with oil decline, giving the Fed room to stay patient rather than hike; supports equities but tight HY spreads and low VIX leave asymmetric risk to widening/volatility on hawkish surprises.
Dollar supported by widening rate differentials but speculative DX longs at 99th percentile cap upside; gold pressured by higher real rates and hawkish Fed.
Breakevens anchored with Fed emphasizing 'will deliver price stability'; little directional edge.
Fiscal/supply lens: large structural deficits keep coupon supply heavy; early-August quarterly refunding is a near-term focal point for duration supply and term premium.
Desk notes ownership shift from price-insensitive official holders to price-sensitive private investors, implying upward pressure on term premium at the long end.
Front end anchored by low bill supply and Fed reserve-management bill purchases; 2y driven mainly by policy expectations, so little fiscal edge there.
2s10s near 5th percentile of its 1y range after front-end-led flattening; term-premium rebuild argues for modest steepening over 1-3 months.
Heavy AI-related corporate bond issuance plus Treasury supply competes for duration buyers; HY spreads near 1y tights have mild upside skew over 3m.
Higher term premium is a mild headwind for equity valuations but not enough to override positive drift; fiscal-debasement support for gold is offset by its strong downtrend.
Financial conditions are loose: NFCI -0.52, HY OAS 2.69 near 1y lows, VIX ~15; Fed balance sheet edging up via reserve management bill purchases keeps reserves ample.
Money markets soft (repo dipped below IORB in May, ON RRP take-up); no funding stress signal near term, supporting risk assets and carry.
Tight spreads and low VIX leave little cushion; private credit/BDC redemption pressure is a slow-burn risk that skews 3m spread and VIX odds modestly higher.
Dollar speculative longs at 99th percentile limit further upside; rate differentials already priced.
Front-end yields near 1y highs with hike priced for 2027; ample liquidity and falling oil argue mild mean reversion lower rather than further rise.
Equities supported by liquidity, AI capex financing via solid issuance; momentum intact.
Complacency signals: VIX 15 (10th pct), HY OAS 2.69 (5th pct), NFCI loose; VX spec short -64k leaves room for vol and spread mean reversion over 1-3m.
Dollar-index spec longs at 99th percentile (+25% of OI) are crowded, tilting the broad dollar toward downside on reversal.
ES spec net short only at 93rd percentile (light shorts) with equities at highs; momentum supports SPX but upside edge is trimmed by stretched sentiment.
WTI spec length cut sharply (-35k, 30th pct) after a 23% monthly drop; washed-out positioning gives a mild contrarian bounce bias.
Gold at 3rd percentile price but specs still heavily long (52% of OI, 45th pct); no capitulation yet, so no contrarian buy signal.
Treasury positioning is neutral (TY 51st pct) while TU shorts are being covered; yields near 1y highs and the 2s10s near 1y lows suggest mild mean reversion lower in yields and steeper curve.
The ECB has hiked and markets price further hikes in the euro area and UK. With the US 2y already at its 1y high and a 2027 Fed hike priced, US-foreign rate gaps have limited room to widen further.

Speculative positioning in dollar index futures is at the 99th percentile, so the long-dollar trade is crowded. The US-Iran memorandum and the oil drop ease the terms-of-trade squeeze on Europe and Asia. Together these lean modestly toward a softer broad dollar.
A softer dollar and gold at the 3rd percentile of its 1y range give a mild upward bias to gold, though the momentum is negative.

Foreign growth is weak in Europe and Canada while high-tech Asia is booming on the AI buildout. Global AI capex and earnings momentum support US equities, and calmer geopolitics keeps the VIX and HY spreads low, though both are already near their 1y lows.

Rising sovereign yields abroad and the shift in Treasury ownership toward price-sensitive private investors support the term premium. That argues for mild curve steepening rather than a large move in the 10y level.
Oil has partly unwound its Hormuz premium. The global supply normalization skews risks mildly lower over 1-3m, but the risk that the deal fails keeps this near a coin flip.

US-Iran MOU and prospective Hormuz reopening drove WTI down ~23% in a month from a 114 peak; returning Gulf supply and inventory rebuild argue for further drift lower, though the 1w +3.9% bounce and re-escalation tail limit conviction.
Speculative crude length cut sharply (30th pct), reducing liquidation risk but signaling no bullish catalyst; staff expects retail gasoline to decline in H2.
Fading energy shock eases headline inflation pressure and hawkish Fed risk, mildly bearish for 2y/10y yields from near 1y highs; breakevens at 10th pct already reflect much of this.
Gold at 3rd percentile after -15% in 3m as risk premium unwound and real rates rose; positioning neutral, so roughly balanced with slight mean-reversion tilt at 3m.
Lower energy costs support margins and consumers, favoring equities and tight HY spreads, though spreads near 1y lows leave limited room; VIX near lows with modest upside skew over longer horizons.

The US-Iran memorandum of understanding and the agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have largely stripped the geopolitical premium out of oil (-23% in 1m), gold (-15% in 3m) and near-term breakevens.

The base case is that the deal holds and supply flows normalise, which keeps a mild downward bias on WTI over 3m. The tail risk, however, is re-escalation and implementation hiccups, which would lift oil, breakevens and the VIX and widen spreads; this skews risk assets' tails negatively.

The VIX at 15 and HY spreads at their 5th percentile leave little room for geopolitical or political surprises. Midterm campaign season and tariff headlines within the 3m window argue for a modest upward drift in volatility and spreads.
Equities have strong AI and earnings momentum and peace-driven relief; absent a shock, the drift remains upward.

Rates are mainly a Fed story (hawkish tilt under Chair Warsh, easing bias removed). Geopolitics is roughly neutral for yields now that the energy shock is fading, with a slight downside tilt for front-end yields as headline inflation from energy recedes.
The dollar was supported by rate differentials and conflict-era safe-haven demand. Easing tensions and an extremely long speculative DX position point to a slight downside bias.

thesis: The Fed is on a hawkish hold at 3.50-3.75%. It has dropped its easing bias, and a few participants already argue for hikes. The 2y yield sits at the 99th percentile of its 1y range, with a hike priced for mid-2027. The 23% oil drop after the US-Iran MoU should soften headline inflation, and June payrolls were soft at +57k. Together these give mild downside skew to front-end yields over 1-3 months. The 10y is held up by term premium, heavy supply and a shift in Treasury ownership toward price-sensitive private investors, so modest bull steepening from 2s10s near its 1y low is the likelier curve move. Equities have AI and earnings momentum, loose financial conditions (NFCI -0.52) and lower energy costs, so the upward drift is intact. HY spreads at their 5th percentile and the VIX at its 10th percentile give little room to fall further. That skews 1-3 month risks toward wider spreads and higher vol, with mean reversion offsetting the usual drift. Crowded speculative dollar longs (99th percentile) and narrowing rate differentials tilt the dollar slightly lower. Oil is roughly balanced: supply normalization leans lower, but washed-out positioning and re-escalation risk lean higher. Gold is near neutral: its downtrend and higher real rates are offset by a softer dollar and its 3rd-percentile level. Breakevens have no edge.
